properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: hash.js ships in node_modules with the dev toolchain. Its SHA-1/SHA-2 streams back web3's internal hashing; the published dist token lists contain no cryptography. Quantum-unsafe tag stems from the SHA-1 member of the family — low urgency (Grover only).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the secp256k1 ECDSA package ships in the dev toolchain via web3; the repo's own code reaches keccak/secp256k1 only indirectly (see the reported web3-utils wrapper finding). Deadline-classical risk only — no live key material here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: npm package evp_bytestokey (implements OpenSSL's legacy single-round MD5 EVP_BytesToKey KDF) in the resolved dependency tree: required by browserify-aes ^1.0.3 and browserify-cipher ^1.0.0, part of crypto-browserify pulled in by the web3 devDependency. Lockfile presence only — no first-party call site; records what the installed tree ships. Changeable here via dependency updates.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: bcrypt-pbkdf is genuine crypto (OpenBSD's bcrypt-based KDF used for ssh private-key derivation), shipped with the dev toolchain. No live password hashing or key derivation happens in this repo's own code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CORRECTED ORIGIN: @noble/curves@1.9.7 is a PRODUCTION dependency, pulled by @solana/web3.js@1.98.4 (declared but not required by any first-party script); also reachable through web3's ethereum-cryptography chain. secp256k1 (Ethereum's signing curve) is one of the curves the library ships. Quantum-unsafe signature primitive (Shor); deadline risk. Installed-tree presence — no first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the ECDH polyfill ships with the dev toolchain; it would only execute inside browserified builds of web3, which this repo never produces. Harvest-now-decrypt-later class if ever exercised, but no session is initiated from this codebase.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CORRECTED ORIGIN: @noble/curves@1.9.7 is a PRODUCTION dependency, pulled by @solana/web3.js@1.98.4 (declared in package.json but not required by any first-party script) — it supplies Ed25519 for Solana Keypairs and secp256k1 for address derivation. Same library also reachable through web3's toolchain. Quantum-unsafe signature primitive (Shor); deadline risk. Installed-tree presence — no first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA as implemented by elliptic@6.5.4 (provides secp256k1/secp256r1 ECDSA), a transitive dependency of the web3 devDependency tree (ethereumjs-util and friends). Signature-class quantum risk. Installed-tree presence only — no first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/curves ships with the published build (runtime dependency). Presence is the question this inventory answers; curve selection lives inside @solana/web3.js, and is observable here rather than changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 scalar multiplication (crypto_scalarmult) as provided by tweetnacl@0.14.5, transitive dependency via sshpk@1.17.0 → bcrypt-pbkdf@1.0.2 (the request/http-signature library tree, required by checkLogos.js). Key-agreement-class quantum risk. Installed-tree presence only — no first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (SHA-3 family) packages in the resolved dependency tree: @ethersproject/keccak256 ^5.7.0 and keccak ^3.0.0, transitive dependencies of web3 / @solana/web3.js tooling. This is the hash behind Ethereum EIP-55 address checksums, and it is the one primitive the app actually exercises at runtime — via web3.utils.toChecksumAddress in the build scripts (see separate finding for the call chain).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2 and @types/pbkdf2 npm packages in the resolved dependency tree (pbkdf2 required by crypto-browserify under web3's dependency chain; @types/pbkdf2 pulled alongside). Lockfile presence — no first-party call site; the KDF ships in the installed tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: scrypt-js ships with the dev toolchain; it would derive keys only inside web3's account/keystore code, which this repo never exercises. scrypt is memory-hard and Grover-only — low PQ urgency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/hashes ships with the published build (runtime dependency via @solana/web3.js); hashing happens inside the library, never in this repo's own code. SHA-256 is PQ-adequate for most purposes; no weakness beyond the group's general tags.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CORRECTED ORIGIN: @noble/hashes@1.8.0 is a PRODUCTION dependency, pulled by @solana/web3.js@1.98.4 (declared but not required by any first-party script; the library itself is not in the shard's site list but its capability is what this object records). BLAKE3 ships in the installed tree; hash-class primitive (Grover only). No first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CORRECTED ORIGIN: @noble/hashes@1.8.0 is a PRODUCTION dependency, pulled by @solana/web3.js@1.98.4 (declared but not required by any first-party script); also reachable through web3's toolchain. SHA-3/Keccak ships in the installed tree — distinct from the keccak/@ethersproject packages under ALG-052c24b2, which the app exercises for EIP-55 checksums. No first-party call site for the noble variant.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: XSalsa20-Poly1305 (crypto_secretbox) as provided by tweetnacl@0.14.5, transitive dependency via sshpk → bcrypt-pbkdf (request library tree). AE-class primitive, not quantum-vulnerable in the Shor sense; presence records what the installed tree ships. No first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl ships with the dev toolchain only (sshpk chain); its NaCl primitives (secretbox, Ed25519) never run from this repo's code. The published dist token lists carry no cryptography.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CORRECTED ORIGIN: crypto library @noble/hashes@1.8.0, a PRODUCTION dependency of @solana/web3.js@1.98.4 (sha2/sha3/keccak/blake2/blake3/ripemd/pbkdf2/scrypt) — also required by web3's toolchain. The library ships in the installed tree; no first-party script calls it directly (the app's keccak use runs through web3.utils, not noble's API).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: this is the EC-crypto provider of the published build. The algorithms it exposes (secp256k1, ed25519, P-256, X25519) are what @solana/web3.js uses for transaction signature verification; presence is the asset, since the repo's data is consumed by wallets that verify those signatures.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto dependency scrypt-js@3.0.1 (scrypt memory-hard KDF), transitive in the web3 dependency tree (required by web3-eth-accounts' key-derivation chain). Lockfile presence — no first-party call site; scrypt ships in the installed tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: sha.js ships with the dev toolchain (via web3/browserify); note 2.4.11 is an old release (current 2.4.12) but ships only SHA-1/SHA-2 members, whose weakness profile is Grover-only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto dependency elliptic@6.5.4 — ECDSA/ECDH over secp256k1 and other curves; transitive dependency of the web3 tree (ethereumjs-util etc.). The library ships in the installed tree; no first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto dependency hash.js@1.1.7 (sha256/sha512/ripemd160 and other hash implementations), transitive dependency of the web3 tree (ethereumjs-util at line 378 requires it). Lockfile presence — no first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto dependency pbkdf2@3.1.2 (PBKDF2 KDF, part of the crypto-browserify shim stack under web3). Lockfile presence — no first-party call site; same logical package as the pbkdf2 entries under ALG-4de3b020's sites, recorded here as the shipped library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: First-party transport key exchange, changeable here: the build's fetch to nodes.mewapi.io rides Node default TLS — classical X25519 ECDHE today, PQ hybrid only if the build image's Node is ≥24.5.0. Pinning the Node version (engines/.nvmrc) would make the PQ posture decided rather than unknown. Two sibling node-fetch sessions (generateFromCoingecko.js, generateMissingTokenListFromIcons.js) are reported separately — this object's single site covers only generateSolMasterFile.js.
